title: Compound Interest Basics
text: Compound interest is interest earned on both principal and previously earned interest. The Rule of 72 estimates doubling time: divide 72 by the annual rate. At 6%, money doubles in about 12 years. Key drivers: rate, time, compounding frequency, and contributions. Starting early beats starting large — 10 years of extra compounding outweighs higher later deposits. Watch fees: a 1% annual fee can consume ~25% of returns over 30 years.
